title: Exchange maps of the Frobenius square
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in the chosen
algebraic closure $\Qlb$, an integer $n\geq1$, and a coefficient ring
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with finite-level coefficient
category the finite-torsion constructible category
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and the integral, rational and
$\Qlb$ categories of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a
separated finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] morphism of
finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with base change $f:X\to Y$ to $k$, let
$g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\Spec(\gamma)$ and
$g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma)$, $\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$,
be the geometric Frobenii [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], and let
$\square_{f}=(f,f,g_Y,g_X,(g_X,f))$ be the Frobenius square of $f_0$, a
Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] by
[lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian]. Use the derived pullback
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the derived direct image
[def-weil-derived-direct-image], the extension by zero
[def-weil-extension-by-zero] and the compact-support direct image
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].

1. *Direct-image exchange.* For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and
$K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$,

$$
 \operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}(K):Lg_Y^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf_*Lg_X^*K
$$

is the ambient exchange transformation $\Ex^{A}_{\square_f}(K)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] for the coefficient sheaf
$R=(A_{E,n})$: the mate, under $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, of
$Lf^*Lg_Y^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_X^*Lf^*Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{Lg_X^*(\varepsilon_K)}Lg_X^*K$, whose first arrow is the
identification $\theta_{\square_f}$ of the square and $\varepsilon$ the
counit of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. For the higher coefficient stages use the following ordered coefficient passage, for the operations and their comparison maps of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. For an integral object $K^\circ\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ put
$$
K_m^\circ=K^\circ\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,m}
$$
using [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Restrict finite-level modules to the completed integral coefficient sheaf using $\operatorname{Res}_m$ of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Form the exchange on the strict coefficient diagram by the same pullback-composition isomorphism and unit/counit mate formula as above, applied before taking the inverse limit. Precisely, on each corner $T$ use the category $\mathscr S_T$ of strict semilinear systems of $B_{T,m}=(A_{E,m})_T$-modules: a transition $M_{m+1}\to M_m$ is linear along $B_{T,m+1}\to B_{T,m}$. Use the simultaneous derived operations, units, counits and mates of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], applied to these coefficient ring systems. Their pullbacks are termwise inverse images, since the finite coefficient sheaves are constant. Let $\mathcal R_XK^\circ$ be represented by $(P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}}B_{X,m})_m$ for one K-flat resolution $P$ of $K^\circ$, with its quotient-induced transitions. Let $\mathcal G_T$ be pullback along $g_T$ on these systems and $\mathcal F_f$ the derived system direct image. The system mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is a specified map
$$
 e_f:\mathcal G_Y\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_XK^\circ
 \longrightarrow\mathcal F_f\mathcal G_X\mathcal R_XK^\circ
 \quad\text{in }D(\mathscr S_Y),
$$
whose evaluation at $m$ is the finite exchange on $K_m^\circ$. This construction specifies the system map before evaluation.

Let $U_Y$ restrict each level along $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to B_{Y,m}$; this is an exact functor to strict towers of completed-coefficient modules, since exactness of systems is componentwise and restriction is exact [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact]. Put $\mathcal L_Y=R\varprojlim\circ U_Y$, using the strict-tower derived inverse-limit functor [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. Write the canonical operation comparisons as
$$
 \alpha_*:Lg_Y^*Rf_*K^\circ\xrightarrow{\sim}
 \mathcal L_Y(\mathcal G_Y\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_XK^\circ),\qquad
 \beta_*:\mathcal L_Y(\mathcal F_f\mathcal G_X\mathcal R_XK^\circ)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*Lg_X^*K^\circ.
$$
They are formed on the simultaneous system models using the integral operation definitions and their reduction comparisons [lem-fix-operation-reduction], including the specified units and counits. Here $f$ is a finite-type $k$-morphism, so integral direct image has its required bounded constructible domain [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible]; the semilinear maps $g_X,g_Y$ are scheme isomorphisms, so their integral pullbacks preserve this domain [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Define
$$
 \operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}(K^\circ)
 =\beta_*\circ\mathcal L_Y(e_f)\circ\alpha_*.
$$
Thus finite reduction of this integral map is the specified finite exchange, via the reduction comparisons; it is not a morphism chosen only from that property.

For $K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)=D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$, use its integral object representative $K^\circ$ and take the image of $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}(K^\circ)$ under scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ represented by $(E',K_{E'})$, for a finite extension $E'/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$, take the morphism class represented by $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*,E'}(K_{E'})$ in the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The scalar-extension comparisons are those of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], and compatible transformations descend as in [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors]. In particular only integral objects are reduced modulo $\varpi^m$; rational objects are handled by scalar localization. No idempotent completion is taken.

2. *Compact-support exchange.* Choose a compactification
$X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X_0\xrightarrow{p_0}Y_0$ of $f_0$ over $k_0$
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements], which exists by
[prop-compactification-refinement]. Its base change
$X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ to $k$ is a compactification
$c$ of $f$ ($j$ is an open immersion and $p$ is proper, properness following from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], while the base change of the open subscheme $X_0\subset\overline X_0$ is the open subscheme $X\subset\overline X$). Put
$g_{\overline X}=\operatorname{id}_{\overline X_0}\times\Spec(\gamma)$. By
[lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian] for $p_0$, the square
$\square_p=(p,p,g_Y,g_{\overline X},(g_{\overline X},p))$ is Cartesian, and
by [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square] for $j_0$ so is the square
$(j,j,g_{\overline X},g_X)$; let
$b_{g_{\overline X}}:Lg_{\overline X}^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!Lg_X^*$ be the
isomorphism of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] for the latter square. For
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and $K$ in the domain of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], with the chosen-compactification notation
$Rf_!^cK=Rp_*j_!K$,

$$
 \operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}^c(K):Lg_Y^*Rp_*j_!K
 \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{FrEx}_{p,*}(j_!K)\ }
 Rp_*Lg_{\overline X}^*j_!K
 \xrightarrow{\ Rp_*(b_{g_{\overline X}}(K))\ }
 Rp_*j_!Lg_X^*K ,
$$

where $\operatorname{FrEx}_{p,*}$ is the direct-image exchange of item 1 for
$\square_p$. This defines $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}^c:Lg_Y^*Rf_!^c\to Rf_!^cLg_X^*$, the chosen-compactification exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c$ of [def-exchange-projection] for the Frobenius square. Here the reference to [def-exchange-projection] identifies its explicit ambient mate and compactification-relative recipe. The displayed Frobenius composite is defined by the ambient ringed exchange and the open-square isomorphism just specified, without treating $g_Y$ as a $k$-morphism or requiring the geometric fibers to be finite type over $k_0$.

For the etale-origin domain, if $K\cong\nu_X^*L$ with $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_{E,n})$, then
$$
 Lg_X^*K\cong\nu_X^*g_{X,\mathrm{et}}^{-1}L
$$
by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], where $\nu_X^*$ is inverse image from the etale to the pro-etale site and $g_{X,\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ is the etale inverse image along $g_X$. Exact inverse image preserves the lower bound, so this specifies an etale-origin witness for $Lg_X^*K$ as well. If a different compactification $d$ was used to define $Rf_!$, transport this specified map on that domain by the comparison isomorphisms $C_{d,c}:Rf_!^d\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!^c$ of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]: the transported map is
$$
(C_{d,c}(Lg_X^*K))^{-1}\circ\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}^c(K)\circ Lg_Y^*(C_{d,c}(K)).
$$
The choice $c$ remains part of this construction. Independence of this transformation from $c$ requires compatibility of the exchange with refinement comparisons, beyond the comparison of the underlying functors.

For integral coefficients use $Rf_!$ of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. On the semilinear system models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], write $\mathcal J_j$ for exact open extension and form the specified composite
$$
 e_f^c:\mathcal G_Y\mathcal F_p\mathcal J_j\mathcal R_XK^\circ
 \xrightarrow{e_p\mathcal J_j}
 \mathcal F_p\mathcal G_{\overline X}\mathcal J_j\mathcal R_XK^\circ
 \xrightarrow{\mathcal F_p(b)}
 \mathcal F_p\mathcal J_j\mathcal G_X\mathcal R_XK^\circ.
$$
Here $b$ is the open-adjunction exchange supplied on the same system models; its finite evaluation is the canonical $b_{g_{\overline X}}$ above. For the canonical operation comparisons
$$
 \alpha_!:Lg_Y^*Rf_!^cK^\circ\xrightarrow{\sim}
 \mathcal L_Y(\mathcal G_Y\mathcal F_p\mathcal J_j\mathcal R_XK^\circ),\qquad
 \beta_!:\mathcal L_Y(\mathcal F_p\mathcal J_j\mathcal G_X\mathcal R_XK^\circ)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!^cLg_X^*K^\circ,
$$
formed using [lem-fix-operation-reduction] on these simultaneous models, define
$$
 \operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}^c(K^\circ)
 =\beta_!\circ\mathcal L_Y(e_f^c)\circ\alpha_!.
$$
The bounded integral output is supplied by [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible]. Rationalize on integral representatives and then take common-stage morphism classes for $\Qlb$ exactly as in item 1. This uses the same compactification $c$ at every finite level.

Both $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}$ and the chosen $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}^c$ are natural
transformations, being composites of natural transformations. The case used
for cohomology is $Y_0=\Spec k_0$, $f_0=a_{X_0}$, $f=a_X:X\to s=\Spec k$,
$g_Y=g_s=\Spec(\gamma)$, written $\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,*}$ and
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,!}$ once this compactification model is fixed. That these maps are isomorphisms is not part of
this definition (part 2 of [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso]
for $f=a_X$).

split_report.summary: Audited the definition against the two Frobenius object definitions and the general exchange definitions in the slopmaster2 source. All constituent notions already exist; no new nodes. Corrected the undefined reduction of rational objects to reduction of integral representatives followed by scalar localization and common-stage passage, explicitly specified diagram-level mates before functorial derived limit, and retained the chosen compactification instead of inferring exchange/refinement compatibility from functor coherence. The ambient Frobenius formula is stated without falsely treating geometric fibers as finite type over k_0 or Galois Frobenius as k-linear. Independent second reading replaced the insufficient constant-ring diagram-site citation by the existing simultaneous semilinear-system calculus, specified exact scalar restriction before total limit, displayed both integral comparison composites, and cited the bounded-domain preservation statements.

This is a definition, so proof and proof_deps remain empty.
